observations.label: Gross rental revenue

working.basis: authority: filed return over borrower statement

steps.text: Pointed to the gross rents line in Birchview Flats - Income Statement, Year Ended December 31, 2025 and in Form 8825 (rental real estate, tax return).
Same property and period (2025-01-01 to 2025-12-31): 512,400 vs 522,000, a difference of 9,600.
Working value 522,000 from Form 8825 (rental real estate, tax return): a filed return outranks a borrower-prepared statement for the same period (example policy).

NOI bridge: statement NOI 328,600 vs Form 8825 line 19 42,500, a gap of 286,100. Catalog bridges explain 295,700 (interest 151,200, depreciation 141,500 (ties: 8825 line 14 = 4562 line 22 = 141500), amortization 3,000 (ties: inside 8825 line 17)). Of the -9,600 left, this line accounts for 9,600.

Investigator suggestion (unverified, cannot resolve the card): The $9,600 difference is likely due to a cash‑basis vs. accrual‑basis timing difference – the owner’s cash‑basis income statement (e1) records rent received in 2025, while the tax return (e0) includes rent earned but not yet collected (or vice‑versa).

hypothesis.hypothesis: The $9,600 difference is likely due to a cash‑basis vs. accrual‑basis timing difference – the owner’s cash‑basis income statement (e1) records rent received in 2025, while the tax return (e0) includes rent earned but not yet collected (or vice‑versa).
steps: Obtain the 2025 rent roll showing lease start/end dates and scheduled rent amounts
Compare rent roll to actual cash receipts in bank statements for 2025
Identify any rent that was earned in 2025 but collected in 2026 (or collected in 2025 but earned in 2024)
Reconcile the amounts to see if the $9,600 gap is explained by these timing items
hypothesis.verify_with: Rent roll for 2025 (or a detailed schedule of rent earned vs. cash received)
